title: Purine Nucleotide Metabolism
objectives: Trace the de novo biosynthesis pathway of purines
Compare purine salvage pathways and their importance
Explain the regulation of purine synthesis and degradation
Diagnose and manage disorders of purine metabolism

overview.title: Purine Metabolism Overview
overview.content:
Purine Production Pathways

  • De novo synthesis: Builds purines from simple precursors (glycine, glutamine, aspartate, CO2, formate)
  • Salvage pathway: Recycles free bases (hypoxanthine, guanine, adenine) via HGPRT/APRT
  • Shared precursor: PRPP (ribose-5-P + ATP)

de_novo.title: De Novo Purine Synthesis
de_novo.content:
10-Step Biosynthesis (Cytosol)

1. PRPP Formation

  • Ribose-5-P + ATP → PRPP (PRPP synthetase)
  • Regulated: Inhibited by ADP/GDP

2. Commitment Step

  • PRPP + glutamine → 5-phosphoribosylamine (PRA) via glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase
  • Key regulation: Inhibited by IMP/AMP/GMP

3-10. IMP Synthesis

  • Glycine, formate (N10-formyl-THF), glutamine, CO2, and aspartate are added stepwise
  • Final product: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
  • Multienzyme complex: Purinosome

AMP & GMP Formation

  • AMP: IMP + aspartate + GTP → adenylosuccinate → AMP
  • GMP: IMP → XMP (NAD+-dependent) → GMP (glutamine + ATP)
  • Reciprocal regulation: GTP for AMP synthesis, ATP for GMP synthesis

salvage.title: Purine Salvage Pathways
salvage.content:
Recycling of Purines

1. HGPRT Pathway

  • Hypoxanthine/guanine + PRPP → IMP/GMP (HGPRT enzyme)
  • Lesch-Nyhan syndrome: HGPRT deficiency → uric acid accumulation

2. APRT Pathway

  • Adenine + PRPP → AMP (APRT enzyme)
  • Deficiency causes 2,8-dihydroxyadenine stones

catabolism.title: Purine Degradation
catabolism.content:
Uric Acid Production

Key Steps

  • AMP → IMP → hypoxanthine → xanthine
  • GMP → guanine → xanthine
  • Xanthine → uric acid (xanthine oxidase)
  • Final product: Uric acid (excreted in urine)

Regulation

  • Xanthine oxidase: Inhibited by allopurinol (gout treatment)
  • Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP): Deficiency causes immunodeficiency

disorders.title: Clinical Disorders
disorders.content:
Purine Metabolic Diseases

1. Gout

  • Cause: Hyperuricemia (>6.8 mg/dL) → urate crystal deposition
  • Triggers: PRPP overproduction, HGPRT deficiency, renal underexcretion
  • Treatment: Allopurinol (XO inhibitor), febuxostat, probenecid

2. Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome

  • Defect: HGPRT deficiency (X-linked recessive)
  • Features: Hyperuricemia, self-mutilation, dystonia, intellectual disability
  • Management: Allopurinol (reduces uric acid), no cure for neurological symptoms

3. ADA/PNP Deficiency

  • Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency: SCID (T/B cell dysfunction)
  • Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency: T-cell immunodeficiency
  • Treatment: Enzyme replacement, bone marrow transplant

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
FAQs

Q: Why does HGPRT deficiency cause neurological symptoms? +

A: Accumulated PRPP increases de novo purine synthesis, leading to excessive uric acid and depletion of GTP/dopamine precursors in basal ganglia.

Q: How does allopurinol treat gout? +

A: It inhibits xanthine oxidase, reducing uric acid production while increasing soluble xanthine/hypoxanthine excretion.

Q: Why do ADA/PNP defects cause immunodeficiency? +

A> Toxic dATP/dGTP accumulate, inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase and blocking DNA synthesis in lymphocytes.
